flashcard_questions.q: What does the word worship come from in Old English?
flashcard_questions.a: “Worthship” — recognising that God is worthy of praise.

flashcard_questions.q: What is liturgical worship in Christianity?
flashcard_questions.a: A church service that follows the same set pattern every time.

flashcard_questions.q: Who leads a liturgical church service?
What is non-liturgical worship in Christianity?
flashcard_questions.a: A service with no fixed order that can change each week.

flashcard_questions.q: What is charismatic worship in Christianity?
flashcard_questions.a: Free-flowing worship led by the Holy Spirit, often with modern music.

flashcard_questions.q: What makes Quaker worship different from Anglican worship?
flashcard_questions.a: Quakers worship in silence with no leader, speaking only when moved.

flashcard_questions.q: What is private worship in Christianity?
flashcard_questions.a: When a Christian praises God alone, often through prayer or Bible reading.

flashcard_questions.q: Which verse teaches Christians to pray behind a closed door?
flashcard_questions.a: Matthew 6:6 — “go into your room, close the door and pray to your Father.”

flashcard_questions.q: What does the S stand for in the prayer acronym STOP?
What does the O stand for in the prayer acronym STOP?
What is a set prayer in Christian worship?
flashcard_questions.a: A written prayer used repeatedly by many Christians.

flashcard_questions.q: What is informal prayer in Christian worship?
flashcard_questions.a: Prayer made up by the believer in their own words.

flashcard_questions.q: Why did Jesus teach the Lord’s Prayer to his disciples?
flashcard_questions.a: They asked him how they should pray.

flashcard_questions.q: Which line of the Lord’s Prayer asks God to provide for daily needs?
What does “hallowed be your name” mean in the Lord’s Prayer?
flashcard_questions.a: God’s name is holy and should be treated with reverence.

notes: 15 cards: 6 term→definition (worthship, liturgical, non-liturgical, charismatic, private worship, set prayer, informal prayer), 2 denomination→position (Quaker worship, who leads liturgical), 2 belief→source (Matthew 6:6, why Jesus taught the Lord’s Prayer), 3 practice→meaning (STOP letters, daily bread, hallowed). Did not list the churches that use each style — that only works as an enumeration.
